title: How Dagobert grew Logology from 200 to 4,000 Twitter followers while bootstrapping
summary: Dagobert, co-founder of Logology (automated designer-quality logos for startups), talks about bootstrapping on savings after 18 months of building and ~5 sales a month. He explains how a spammy tweet led him to Twitter and the daily interaction routine that grew his audience, plus lessons on branding, pricing tiers and signup friction.

principles.text: On Twitter, spend about 10x more time interacting with others than on your own tweets.
principles.quote: you need to spend 10 times more 10 times more time on interacting with others than your own tweets

principles.text: Replies and likes put you in people's feeds for days, so consistent genuine interaction compounds your reach.
principles.quote: as soon as someone interacts with you so like they reply back or they like one of your reply to their content as soon as they do this you know that within 24 48 72 hours you're gonna show up in their feed

principles.text: Twitter beats small communities like Reddit or Indie Hackers for traffic because of its viral component.
principles.quote: it has way more power than like a community like in the hikers or like credit like there's a viral component to it that's huge

principles.text: Sharing your real emotions and frustrations publicly can hook an audience and open doors.
principles.quote: well if i share my emotions and if i share what i feel on twitter it can hook people

principles.text: You don't need a great brand to succeed, but look decent; a brand you love gives confidence and a starting edge.
principles.quote: you need to look at least decent and the second thing is usually when you get a brand that you really love for yourself it gives you a ton of confidence and it gives you a good starting point

principles.text: Removing the signup wall before showing value was what finally produced real sales.
principles.quote: just removing the need to sign up it finally got us some actual sales
